1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e3 e6 5.Nf3.strategy: Develops the bishop to its best diagonal and invites Black to take the pawn. After the capture White retakes and plays for the central advance, while Black grabs queenside space with tempo on the bishop. A rich, double-edged game: White gets the centre, Black the queenside.

Takes the pawn and clears d5, giving up the centre for queenside expansion and time against the bishop. With ...a6 already played, the pawn push against the bishop is ready at once. Black then plays to free the c8-bishop by striking at White's centre.
